The present writ petition has been filed for issuance of direction upon the respondents to follow the procedure of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act, 2013') for acquisition of the petitioner's land appertaining to Khata No. 47, Plot No. 100, measuring an area of 0.43 acre and Plot No. 102, measuring an area of 0.29 acre (in total 0.72 acre), Village Bande, Thana No. 41, PO & PS- Murhu, District Khunti.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Further prayer has been made for issuance of direction upon the respondents to pay adequate compensation to the petitioner for unlawfully occupying the said land.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the land in question originally belonged to Chudka Munda and others and the same has been recorded in the revisional survey record of rights as 'Bakasht Land'.
Thereafter, the aforesaid land came in exclusive possession of Chudka Munda after partition among other co-sharers.

After the death of Chudka Munda, his only son namely,
Mogo Munda came in exclusive possession of the land in question.

Thereafter, Mogo Munda died leaving behind his only son- Paulus Dodray, who died leaving behind his only son- Christopall Dodray (the petitioner herein).

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the aforesaid land was taken by the respondents for the period from 1957 to 1964 for the purpose of agriculture exhibition and to demonstrate the use of chemical manure/ fertilizer as also modern farming system.

However, after completion of the said period, the possession of the aforesaid land was taken back by the ancestors of the petitioner and since then the petitioner/his forefathers have been farming over the same.

Recently, the respondents asked the petitioner to vacate the said land and they forcefully dispossessed him from his land for construction of 'Farmers School' as well as execution of various projects without following due procedure of law as laid down under the Act, 2013.

The petitioner represented the respondent no. 3 - the Deputy Commissioner, Khunti ventilating his grievance, but the same was not responded, which has compelled him to file the present writ petition.
4.

Mr. Anup Kumar Agarwal, AC to GA-IV appearing on behalf of the respondents, submits that the petitioner has not annexed any document suggesting restoration of the land in question in favour of his forefather immediately after 1964.

Otherwise also, the petitioner's claim is required to be factually verified by a competent authority and, therefore, if the petitioner files a fresh representation in this regard before the respondent no. 5 - the District Land Acquisition Officer,
Khunti, an appropriate decision will be taken within a timeframe.

5. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and considering the nature of prayer made by the petitioner in the present writ petition, without entering into merit of the case, the petitioner is given liberty to file a fresh representation along with the relevant documents on the present issue before the respondent no. 5.

On receipt of the said representation, the respondent no. 5, on verifying the relevant records and on providing opportunity of hearing to the petitioner/his representative, shall take an appropriate informed decision within eight weeks from the date of filing of the same.
6. The writ petition is disposed of with the aforesaid liberty and direction.
(Rajesh Shankar, J.) Manish Christopall Dodray vs The State Of Jharkhand on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36058205/
